transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really distressing, intrusive memories of a traumatic event that happened about four months ago. These memories just flash into my mind out of nowhere, and I can't seem to make them stop. It has gotten to the point where it's really hard to get through the day.
Can you tell me more about when these intrusive memories started and if they have been constant since the traumatic event or if they've changed in frequency or intensity over the past four months?

They started almost immediately after the event about four months ago. Since then, they have been incredibly frequent and intense, remaining pretty constant and distressing throughout this entire time. They haven't really let up or changed at all.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the traumatic event, and if so, how has this been affecting your daily life?

Yes, I do everything I can to avoid certain places, people, and conversations that remind me of that day. It has really restricted my daily routine because I refuse to go to certain parts of town or see my friends. I mostly just stay home now to keep myself from being triggered.

You mentioned the traumatic event occurred about four months ago, can you tell me if your symptoms have persisted continuously since then, or have you had any periods where they significantly improved or worsened?

Yes, the symptoms have been completely continuous and persistent since the event happened four months ago. I haven't had any periods of improvement or relief at all; it has just been a constant struggle every single day.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including intrusive memories, avoidance behaviors, and constant distress since the traumatic event four months ago, align closely with the diagnostic criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). The continuous and persistent nature of these symptoms over the past four months, without any periods of significant improvement, further supports PTSD as the primary diagnosis. Acute Stress Disorder is less likely because it typically refers to symptoms that last from 3 days to 1 month after the trauma, and the patient's symptoms have persisted well beyond this timeframe, making PTSD a more appropriate diagnosis.
